title: The worktree registry records the branch a worktree was created with and never follows a checkout
description:
Measured on the live database, 2026-09-29: **5 of 53 registry rows disagree with git** about which branch the worktree has checked out.

```
.superzej/worktrees/pantheon-migration-cli/tg-dandy-otter--86de6644...
    db=tg/dandy-otter    git=fix/saml-metadata-collection
.superzej/worktrees/mysage-ms2-.../tg-juicy-marble
    db=tg/juicy-marble   git=feat/ev-intake-melissa-feedback
.superzej/worktrees/life-automation/tg-swift-bamboo
    db=tg/swift-bamboo   git=fix/restore-darwin-outputs
.superzej/worktrees/mysage-ms2-.../tg-frosty-snow
    db=tg/frosty-snow    git=feat/MS2-321-ticketing-demo
.superzej/worktrees/mysage-ms2-.../tg-rad-leaf
    db=tg/rad-leaf       git=fix/MS2-725-clinic-intake-note-scope-service
```

The pattern is uniform: `db` always holds the generated `tg/<name>` the worktree was **created** with, and `git` holds whatever was checked out later. So the row is written once at creation and never reconciled.

`CLAUDE.md` is explicit that **git is the source of truth for worktrees** and the DB is a cache. This is a cache that silently diverges and is never invalidated.

## Why it matters beyond a stale label

Found while tracing the branch-delete no-op (THE-697). `git branch -d` **and** `-D` both refuse a branch that any worktree holds:

```
error: cannot delete branch 'fix/saml-metadata-collection' used by worktree at '.../tg-dandy-otter--86de6644...'
```

The UI offers a delete for any branch that is not the *current* worktree's HEAD (`run.rs` `b.is_head`; `branch_menu` skips delete when `is_head`). It has no notion of "held by another worktree" -- `BranchRow` carries no such field. So it offers deletes git will refuse.

And the registry cannot be used to fix that, because **it names the wrong branch**. On this machine it would report `tg/dandy-otter` as held (it is not -- it deleted cleanly) and `fix/saml-metadata-collection` as free (it is not -- git refuses it). Exactly inverted for that worktree.

## Other surfaces that read this column

Anything deriving behaviour from `worktrees.branch` rather than asking git is wrong by the same amount. Worth auditing: the sidebar's branch label, merged-worktree sweep eligibility (it reasons about whether a branch is merged), `wt list` output, and any dispatch/pipeline logic keyed on a worktree's branch. A sweep that checks the *recorded* branch's merge status is checking the wrong branch.

## Suggested direction

Reconcile on read rather than trying to catch every checkout. A worktree's branch is one `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (or one `git worktree list --porcelain` for all of them at once), which is cheap enough to do on the existing hydration path and does not need a new watcher. If the column stays, it should be treated as a display hint that is refreshed from git, never as an input to a decision.

Note the 5 rows are not corrupt -- they are correct records of history, just not of current state. A migration is not needed; the read path is what needs changing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No surface decides anything from `worktrees.branch` without reconciling against git first.
- [ ] A worktree whose branch was changed outside thegn shows and behaves as its actual branch.
- [ ] A test changes a worktree's branch behind thegn's back and asserts the reconciled value is used.
- [ ] The branch list knows which branches a worktree holds, so a delete that git will refuse is either not offered or explains which worktree holds it (this is the part THE-697 needs).

## Related

* THE-697 -- branch/worktree delete failures; this is why its held-branch check cannot be built on the registry.
* THE-705 -- separate registry/bookkeeping drift (unlanded held branches, stale delivery index).
